newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Prime Budapest office market tightening - Colliers.
newsitem.headline: Prime Budapest office market tightening - Colliers.

text.p: The vacancy rate for prime downtown office space in the Hungarian capital should fall sharply to below 10 percent next year, Colliers International (Hungary) Ltd said in a research report.

"We expect that only 7,000 sq m of new Class A space will be added downtown next year, significantly down from the 29,000 sq m delivered in 1996," the property consulting firm said in its fall research report.
The report said rental and leasing activity in downtown Budapest would be only slightly lower than this year, at just above 20,000 sq m for 1997.

"This will cause a significant decrease in vacancy rates as available space is taken up," the report, released on Thursday, said. "We believe that vacancy rates will fall to 10 percent by mid-year 1997 and could fall as low as eight percent by the end of the year."

Colliers said 9,000 sq m of prime downtown office space was added in Budapest in the first half of 1996 and that 14,000 sq m had been let. Vacancy rates fell from a high of 17.5 percent at the beginning of the year to 13.3 percent as of July 1, the report said. @
It added that there "has been no discernible decrease in rental rates or increase in tenant incentives in the Class A downtown market over the past several months".
Average rents are currently around 40 DM per sq m per month, the report said, with some premium buildings charging 50 DM per sq m and some older buildings charging 35 DM per sq m.
